title: Site release, permissions and restoration scope
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and water-removal work after a flood or water event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a flood-affected building, energise its systems, or certify it as dry, safe or habitable.
learningOutcomes: Identify the site authority, the permissions and the exclusions before any flood restoration scope is set, and separate a customer request, an insurer authorisation and a professional safety clearance.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how to separate a customer request, an insurer authorisation and a professional safety clearance, and how to set a restoration scope from documented authority. It does not authorise entry, restoration, energisation or certification. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Site release, permissions and restoration scope
instruction.body: Site release, permissions and restoration scope need a documented decision based on the facts of the site, not on assumptions. Distinguish an observable condition from a qualified technical determination. A customer request, an insurer authorisation and a professional safety clearance are three separate documents, and none of them can be treated as the others. Start a scope sheet that names the party responsible for access, for utilities and for environmental hazards. Confirm the site authority and the approved procedure, identify who can make the technical decision, set the exclusions, and then collect only the information that can be gathered safely. Record each unresolved uncertainty. Stop work when permission, controls or competent supervision are missing. Produce an access decision that names the approver, the date, the zones, the limits on activity and the unresolved hazards. Never turn an observation into a technical certificate.

procedure: Stop work and keep people out of any area that has not been released.
Record the customer request, the insurer authorisation and the safety clearance as three separate items, and note which are on file.
Name the site controller, the approver, and the party responsible for access, utilities and environmental hazards.
Set the exclusions and the limits on activity in writing.
Issue an access decision with the approver, the date, the zones, the activity limits and the unresolved hazards.
Do not start work while a document required for the activity is still outstanding.

workedExamples.situation: A customer request, an insurer authorisation and a professional safety clearance have all been mentioned, but only the customer's request is on file.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must be established before the scope is set?
workedExamples.reasoning: Treat the three as separate documents. Only the customer's request exists, so the insurer authorisation and the safety clearance are outstanding. Record the scope sheet, the site controller and the outstanding documents. Do not start on the request alone.

workedExamples.situation: A homeowner asks a restoration company to start drying the lounge today, and no site controller has been named.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not start. Name the site controller, record the outstanding documents and set the exclusions first.

equipmentAndPpe: No entry PPE is issued under this lesson.
Scope sheet and access decision register kept with the job file.

commonErrors.error: Starting work on a customer request while the insurer authorisation and safety clearance are missing.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat the three documents as separate and record which are outstanding.

commonErrors.error: Turning an observation into a technical certificate.
commonErrors.prevention: Record observations. Refer technical determinations to the qualified person.

commonErrors.error: Setting a scope without a named approver.
commonErrors.prevention: Name the approver and the date on the access decision.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not authorise entry to a flood-affected building or any restoration work. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
Safe Work Australia's guidance says a PCBU has a primary duty to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety of workers and others affected by the work.
The same guidance says the hierarchy of control can be applied in relation to any risk.

qualityStandard: The learner separates the three documents and names the outstanding ones.
The learner refuses to start work without a named approver and written limits.
documentationEvidence: Scope sheet and access decision: approver, date, zones, activity limits, unresolved hazards.
Register of the customer, insurer and clearance documents with their status.
summary: Customer requests, insurer authorisations and safety clearances are separate.
Scope starts with the documented site authority.
Stop when permission or the site controller is missing.

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer request is on file, but the insurer authorisation and the professional safety clearance are not. What should happen first?
options: Start the work, because the customer has asked and the customer is waiting for the crew to arrive on site
Start the drying and sort out the paperwork later, since the drying cannot wait for the approvals
Record the scope sheet and the outstanding documents, and do not start on the customer request alone.

knowledgeChecks.question: Under Safe Work Australia's guidance, what does the PCBU primary duty cover?
options: The health and safety of workers and others, so far as is reasonably practicable
Only the health of the customer

officialReferences.title: Duties of a person conducting a business or undertaking (PCBU)
officialReferences.covers: Read directly 2026-11-03. A PCBU has a primary duty to ensure the health and safety of workers while they are at work, and must consider others affected by the work, such as visitors. The primary duty requires PCBUs to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the listed measures. The hierarchy of control can be applied in relation to any risk. National model WHS guidance; state or territory adoption to be checked.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a flood-affected building, to carry out regulated flood restoration, to energise or isolate electrical, gas or solar systems, to remove sewage or contaminated water, to dispose of waste, or to certify that a property is dry, hygienic, structurally sound or safe to occupy. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Some of the work described is restricted to licensed, authorised or specially trained people, including electrical and gas work, structural assessment, sewage handling and some disposal. The site controller, the owner, the insurer and the competent professionals each hold separate decisions, and none of them replaces the others. Where the controlling authority or the competent professional is not identified, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: permission to enter or written safety clearance is missing; the contamination is unknown; a structural hazard, a slip or a confined space has not been cleared; an electrical, gas or solar system is water-exposed or has not been licensed for re-energisation; an exposure has occurred or controls are not in place; the equipment or operators are not suitable; porous material is in question; hidden microbial contamination is suspected; a waste route is not yet known; or a party asks for a dry, hygienic or occupancy statement. A stop-work decision is correct. Record it, and restart only after the competent party has confirmed the scope in writing.
